articleTitle: Low-Voltage 60Gb/s NRZ and 100Gb/s PAM4 O-Band Silicon Ring Modulator
abstract: We demonstrate 60Gb/s NRZ and 100Gb/s PAM4 data modulation with an O-band silicon ring modulator with only 1.6V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</sub> and 2.5V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp</sub> drive swing respectively, leveraging the large modulation efficiency (55pm/V) and electro-optical bandwidth (35GHz) realized by an optimized vertical PN diode phase shifter design.

articleTitle: A 112 Gb/s PAM4 CMOS Optical Receiver with Sub-pJ/bit Energy Efficiency
abstract: We present a 112Gb/s PAM4 optical receiver to meet the requirements of emerging 400G Ethernet standards. Our receiver uses a 35GHz Ge-on-Si- Pdwire-bonded to a 28nm CMOS linear TIA. Measurement results verify target performance at 0.96pJ/bit efficiency, showing the potential for low-cost 100+G/λ optical receivers.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Analysis of Frequency Comb Sources for Silicon Photonic Interconnects
abstract: We present a procedure for modeling the energy efficiency of frequency comb sources based on empirical device measurements. The proposed methodology allows for rapid exploration of the joint source-link design space to identify valid configurations that minimize the energy consumption of the link.

articleTitle: A 4×25-Gbps Monolithically Integrated Si Photonic WDM Transmitter with Ring Modulators
abstract: We demonstrate a 100-Gbps (4×25-Gbps) Si Photonic WDM transmitter containing monolithically integrated Si ring modulators (RMs) and BiCMOS driving circuits. Our transmitter is designed with the large-signal circuit model for the Si RM, which allows easy and accurate optimization of the entire WDM transmitter.

articleTitle: Behavioral Model of Silicon Photonics Microring with Unequal Ring and Bus Widths
abstract: Microring resonators (MRR) with non-identical ring and bus waveguide widths are easier to fabricate as they allow for larger gaps. For effective design exploration, we propose a new behavioral model for the directional coupler of an MRR with non-identical ring and bus widths, which can be used to calculate the MRR design performace. The analysis shows that the proposed modeling technique matches the corresponding 3D FDTD simulations well.

articleTitle: Energy Efficiency Analysis of Coherent Links for Datacenters
abstract: We propose that coherent optical communication can offer energy-efficient operation in datacenters. Analysis and simulations determine optimal operating points for the laser and local oscillator (LO) and compare trade-offs in Silicon (Si) and Indium Phosphide (InP) Mach-Zehnder Modulators (MZMs) to reach pJ/b scale efficiency.

articleTitle: High-Performance Single-Mode Polymer Waveguide Devices for Chip-Scale Optical Interconnects
abstract: Here we present next generation polymer-based singlemode waveguide devices and architectures for chip-scale photonic interconnections. A suite of optical devices are developed showing record low propagation loss, high-performance signal/power routing, and high-density inter-layer coupling. Flexible waveguide ribbons are further demonstrated that are widely applicable across chip- and board-domains.

articleTitle: Silicon Microring Modulator with Transparent Conductive Oxide Gate
abstract: We designed a novel microring modulator based on hybrid transparent conductive oxide-silicon metal-oxide-semiconductor (MOS) capacitor. Experimental results achieved large wavelength tunability of 100 pm/V and 3 dB modulation at 3V of V<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">pp.</sub> Analysis indicates that 44 GHz sneed can be achieved by optimizing the electrode design.

articleTitle: Statistical Behavioral Models of Silicon Ring Resonators at a Commercial CMOS Foundry
abstract: We report on statistical behavioral models of silicon ring resonators in a commercial CMOS foundry. Process variability is inferred from optical tests and validated by inline metrology data. Significant reflection is observed on many designs, and the impact of reflection on system integration are discussed.

articleTitle: Frequency Stabilized Lasers for Coherent Fiber Interconnects in the Datacenter (Invited Talk)
abstract: As data center ethernet switches scale towards 100Tbps, the fiber interconnect will face significant cost, power and engineering barriers. We describe FRESCO, a fiber data center interconnect (DCI) that brings highly coherent WDM Terabit links inside the data center without the need for DSPs and other power consuming technologies. FRESCO is based on integrated ultra-stable, ultra-low linewidth laser, frequency comb and silicon photonic transceiver technologies.

articleTitle: A Design Study of Efficiency Enhancement in Silicon Photonic Thermo-Optic Phase Shifters
abstract: We study the process and physical design parameters of a silicon photonic thermo-optic phase shifter with etched air trenches to improve energy efficiency. Multi-physics simulation and measurement results from a test chip generate design guidelines.

articleTitle: Real-Time Digital Subcarrier Cross-Connect Based on Distributed Arithmetic DSP Algorithm
abstract: A real-time DSP enabled digital subcarrier cross-connect (DSXC) with resampling filters is demonstrated based on distributed arithmetic (DA) for channel frequency translation. This circuit-based DSXC supports flexible and fine data-rate granularity of subcarrier channels, and offers the capability to improve spectral efficiency in optical networks.

articleTitle: A 50Gbit/s Net NRZ Error-Free 850nm VCSEL Based Optical Interconnect
abstract: We present an 850nm multimode VCSEL based optical interconnect operating error free with the net data rates up to 50Gbit/s. The transmitter and receiver are fabricated in 130nm BICMOS and the total power consumption of the link goes down to record 4.7pJ/bit at 54Gbit/s.

articleTitle: Time-Efficient Photonic Variability Simulator for Uncertainty Quantification of Photonic Integrated Circuit
abstract: We present a novel simulation platform for uncertainty quantification (UQ) studies of photonic integrated circuit (PIC) design. This platform supports time-efficient variability studies such as stochastic collocation and spectral projection that enables variability aware PIC design.

articleTitle: A Heterogeneously Integrated Silicon Photonic/LiNbO3Electro-Optic Modulator
abstract: We present a heterogeneous CMOS compatible Mach-Zehnder modulator simultaneously utilizing the electro-optic effect in LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub> and taking advantage of the benefits of silicon photonics. Aside from the final step of bonding the LiNbO<sub xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</sub>, this modulator can be entirely fabricated using CMOS facilities.

articleTitle: High-Speed Atto-Joule per Bit Photonic Crystal Nanocavity Modulator
abstract: We quantitatively analyzed the determinant factors for energy efficiency of carrier-driven resonator-based electro-optic modulator and reported an ultra-compact transparent conductive oxides (TCOs) gated silicon photonic crystal nanocavity modulator design, demonstrating high E-O efficiency of 250pm/V, low energy consumption of 3fJ/bit and gigahertz operation speed.

articleTitle: Self-Homodyne 16-QAM Scheme for Low Complexity 200 Gbps Data Center Interconnects
abstract: Polarization multiplexing of carrier with modulated signal to achieve coherent links with LO-free receivers has been proposed. The approach can replace 100-Gbps PAM4 with 200-Gbps self-homodyne 16-QAM links having similar electronics. A practical self-homodyne 16-QAM link with adaptive polarization control has been experimentally demonstrated.

articleTitle: Non-Linear System Identification Scheme for the Design of Efficient Compensators and Calibrations
abstract: The optical transmitter components may cause nonlinear distortions mixed with memory effect. Using a system model identification scheme based on Volterra series, enable distortion root cause identification and design of efficient compensators to mitigate these effects.

articleTitle: Silicon-Plasmonic Electro-Absorption Modulator Gated by High Mobility Indium Oxide
abstract: We apply the quantum model to analyze the free carrier distribution of the ENZ layer of the Au/TCO/HfO2/p-Si capacitor on standard silicon-on-insulator (SOI) waveguides. We also experimentally demonstrated the correlation between the electro-absorption (EA) rate and the mobility of TCO materials, which confirms the accuracy of the quantum model.

articleTitle: Parameters-Insensitive Modulator for Optical Interconnect Systems Based on Double Injection
abstract: A racetrack-shaped ring modulator based on Double Injection (DI) was recently reported. It is capable of delivering a variety of transform functions, and can be designed to exhibit considerably less sensitivity to deviations in parameters. The modulator is referred to as PIR20 - Parameters-Insensitive Response with a minimum extinction ratio of 20dB. The unique properties of the DI approach can override the impact of such deviations so as to obtain an extinction ratio of at least 20dB, which compares favorably with other device architectures. Such deviations may result from fabrication variations and influence sensitive components of the circuit such as coupling structures. In addition, in some architectures, e.g. Silicon Photonics, electro-optical activity generates heat due to carrier transport, which affects the circuit operation. The sensitivity of the PIR20 modulator to deviations in directional couplers and changes in temperature is analyzed and compared to other known modulators based on either a ring, MZI or Fabry-Pérot resonators. The analysis is carried out for Silicon Photonics and reveals that the PIR20 is considerably more robust to both effects compared with other devices. Comprised of only one ring and having a small footprint, makes this modulator an appealing candidate for large scale integration in interconnects systems and RF photonics.

articleTitle: Board-Level Transceiver and Routing Technologies for Chip-to-Chip Optical Interconnect Architectures
abstract: We present the ICT-STREAMS optical interconnect architecture and report on the recent advancements of its O-band silicon photonic key building-blocks namely a 4×40Gbps transmitter and an 8×8 Arrayed Waveguide Grating Router (AWGR) device.

articleTitle: Novel Design for Subterahertz Bandwidth Ultracompact Lithium Niobate Electrooptic Modulators on Silicon
abstract: Ultracompact thin-film lithium-niobate Mach-Zehnder electrooptic modulators on silicon substrate capable of operating up to subterahertz range of the electromagnetic spectrum are devised. Design optimizations for achieving 3-dB bandwidths up to 400 GHz are presented.
